claude.request:
Today's international headlines:
- Curfew imposed in parts of central Paris and other cities after rioting across France: The country's interior minister admits that police "lost control" in some cities following a weekend of riots.
- Ukrainians dying because US restricting intelligence sharing, Zelensky adviser tells BBC: Serhii Beskrestnov says there has not been enough time to warn people about incoming missile attacks. The White House said there had been no changes to intelligence sharing.
- Seventh day of violent clashes between Albanian protesters and police: Almost 300 people have been injured, more than half of them police, as violent anti-government demonstrations show no sign of easing.
- Canadian tourist found guilty of animal cruelty after stealing Las Vegas flamingo from enclosure: The man testified that he snatched Peachy from its enclosure at the Flamingo hotel and casino after drinking 30 to 40 beers, but did not mean any harm.
- Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon: A spacecraft is set to launch on an ambitious mission to bring 10g of Martian moon dust back to Earth.
- Tennis star Svitolina says emotional toll of Ukraine war led to Monfils separation: The two top tennis pros married in 2021 and have one child together.
- Ex-OpenAI worker accused of planting device had Saudi support, says court filing: The Saudi government did not immediately respond to BBC requests for comment.
- Exiled critic of Rwandan president found beheaded: Former army sergeant major Robert Kabera was a popular YouTuber and singer, who had sought asylum in Uganda.
- Houthi missile strike on Yemen camp kills 50 security recruits, local authorities say: Three missiles hit a camp in government-controlled Shabwa province that officials say was being used as a training centre for new recruits.
- Obama blasts federal probe of Ilhan Omar as 'so appalling': Obama says federal agents' search of the Democrat's home was an effort to intimidate a Trump critic.
- US airman dies as daredevil descent goes wrong before Texas college football game: The game continued after the incident. The American Conference said the decision was made before his death was known.
- Personal attacks fire up debate before Brazil's run-off vote: The race heats up just days before the run-off between the left-wing incumbent and his right-wing challenger.
